books.title: Dance Dance Dance
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.review:
Dance Dance Dance what a book !! And by that really what the hell. 

If we Start at Starting , I guess it's bit interesting the premise of it. Though the middle goes no where and end is just terrible.

Keeping in line with other Murakami books it leaves lot more questions unanswered then answered. There is ambiguity almost for the sake of it.

This is one of those book where there isn't a guy or girl obsessed with reading book though there is an author Hiraku M something.

No cats talking but a sheep man.

And I don't think I am inclined for another Murakami now, it's just grrr... Yuki 's character was just, why was it the it was. It was overt sexualization for no reason.

There is no rhyme or reason in the book.

One thing is clear Murakami can write other things may be what the hell is he writing.

I guess my rating would be Norwegian Woods and Kafka on the shore on top followed by 1Q84 and then books like after Dark and Dance Dance Dance at bottom tier.

Grr..I really wanted this book to be more enjoyable but I did finish. But I did finish reading which is more than what I can say for many others I tried this year.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.review:
Two stars for the book is perhaps low, but this was my experience. Not necessarily because the book was bad, but I was expecting something else.


I dived into this after reading Remains of the Day, and this was a big let down compared to that. From the writing to genre to everything it felt like a completely different author.

It didn't help that I wasn't quite expecting a dystopian novel or that I had to read through the entire thing to get the accurate dystopian nature of it.

books.title: Don't Lose Your Mind, Lose Your Weight
books.author: Rujuta Diwekar
books.review:
I am not the one for self help books in general.  And have 0 will power to follow a diet. 

But I got this book gifted accidentally and after 2 years on my shelf, I thought I might as well give it a try.

I do have take away from books, so it was kinda good. 

Let's see if it helps me in being more healthy.

books.title: The Chola Tigers: Avengers of Somnath
books.author: Amish Tripathi
books.review:
I have read and watched historical fiction and have largely enjoyed them. I was s big fan of Amish's Shiva trilogy but wasn't sold on this book. 



Now that I have crossed over 3/4th of book, some of my thoughts.


Large part of the book is about aftermath of Somnath temple destruction a small troop from Chola kingdom to heart land of Ghazni kingdom to assassinate Mahmud Gazni


-Writing can definitely be improved. Compared to some of the other great writers stuff is amateurish. Like current page I am reading has someone from South India a Millenia ago thinking "how much does this bugger know". This just completely breaks the immersion.


- I feel for sure some thing would have been forced by publisher or editor, because you should not have some one in that era in that geography identifyinga as they them. This is a political issue in current arena affair and has no place in book like this. I am ok if you want to showcase someone as transgender because they have existed in India for centuries but not pronoun stuff.



- All fictions take a leap in logic here and there, this one seems bit unnecessary. Devout peope of Abhramaic faith fighting for Ayappa and Lord Shiva was little difficult for me to digest.

 Guy gets paralyzed in right hand and learns to fight almost equally with his left hand in a very short time, people learn entire new language over few weeks with complete fluency.

About 1000 prisoners escape from heavily militarized city and cross desert and all back covering so much distance without being caught.. 


-I like the setting and description of the era of this time. It's almost as if care was taken to write this book with intention of getting a movie made on this. 


- I enjoyed the palace intrigue of Gaznivad quite a bit, probably my favorite arc to read. Though Chola kingdom description also was decent.


-Love story between Vijayan and Amal was just rammed through for sake of movie. There was no need for Amal to be female.


-Turks are shown to be absolute monsters in fact one of the line pretty much says that. It might be true so may be fair.


- I can't believe I am saying but religious refrences from Jain to Buddhists to Muslims to Jains to Christian can sometimes be a bit too much. Fishing lowest common denominator and leaning on all being same should not have been the focus of the book.


- I finished the book and more of above. Last chapter was interesting read. Though I can't fathom India being able to survive the third attack mentioned using the path mentioned. It's just not going to happen.

books.title: Doctor Who: The Clockwise Man
books.author: Justin Richards
books.review:
This was my first foray into the Doctor Who show, movie or book and although the set up was pretty exciting some of the part of the book led me down. 

Freddy's part was rather not required to that extent and also a bit extraordinary.

I tend to rate books and stories solely on misunderstanding often a bit underwhelming (unless it's for humor) so this was disappointing.

books.title: The Secret of Secrets (Robert Langdon, #6)
books.author: Dan    Brown
books.review:
I remember my first Dan Brown book "The Deception Point' having read that I sought to read all of his other novels published till then. imIt always a bit exciting to be able to read a new one and try and capture that joy and excitement of reading this book when I was in high school and first read his book. 


Coming to the book itself it plays largely on the usual formula which is expected now, it also has a  lot of random Information which is sometimes intriguing. 


However , this was not much of a mystery more of a thriller. Whatever mystery there was also revealed quite early and from then on it was a thriller novel and the usual big reveal is not a big reveal but something everyone saw coming and also it doesn't have much impact on the story.

I feel the ending could've been trimmed it was way too long in tying up  all threads.

On a lighter note, Book probably could've done without some of the time checks by Langdon. his 6:00 am to 9:00 am seems to last soo long with so many things crammed in there.

Anyway , it's a typical RL book and if you enjoy it you enjoy it.

books.title: Uncle Fred in the Springtime (Blandings Castle, #6)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
There is not much point in reviewing a Blandings Castle novel by PG Wodehouse.

This was my third reading of the book and the second in less than 365 days, I don't know what it is about this chap that I keep on reading and re- reading all his books so many times.

I have on the shelf two perfectly fine books released this month by two perfectly fine authors , but my mind wanted to give this one another shot. Damn you , P.G.Wodehouse.

Uncle Fred A character worth investing in.

books.title: Guards! Guards! (Discworld, #8; City Watch, #1)
books.author: Terry Pratchett
books.review:
This is largely a fantastic book which didn't work for me. 


Either it's the writing or my reading which had severely impacted my ability to enjoy it and it's probably the later.

Although funny at times, I found writing to be confusing so much so that I not only didn't realise the reversal of the antagonist in the end but for some reading pretty much assumed it was mentioned as someone else earlier in the book.

books.title: Roadside Picnic
books.author: Arkady Strugatsky
books.review:
Sometimes I think my ability to read isn't that refined so many times The classic will leave me disappointed and books which require introspection or lean heavily on inferring something from text are missed heavily by me. ..

This book suggested by an enthusiastic friend of which I had high hopes has been a let down.

The book doesn't explain anything properly The start is a bit too slow and the rest of the book doesn't make up for it. There are different threads which don't go anywhere and it seems like a lot of unfulfilled potential with the premise.

I did not even particularly enjoy the writing. I have no trouble believing this would be a favorite for many and many would swear by it. This though was not for me.

books.title: The Remains of the Day
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.review:
I had, as I often do, fallen in rut of not reading and was looking for a book to get me out of it.

I came across this book and reviews were just glowing. Compared to the reviews, the book was a let down

BUT I did manage to finish it quite quickly and that just goes to show it was a good read apart from typos (which makes me feel like flipkart the seller fleeced me with a pirated copy ). So in some ways it got the work done . One thing I cans ay the writer can write and kept me engaged even for better part.

I expected a lot more on War but what I got was introspection and the opportunity to see someone's life go by in some way.

I have not read or studied about the book intentionally to keep this review honest from my end. I felt the main character Mr. Steven was to an extent unlikable I am not sure if he is meant to be. It also makes me question some of the things we consider important in life, for instance dignity as mentioned in the book. I perhaps should revisit the entire concept. 

As the book says, Evenings after the end of the work day are often the best part and should be celebrated and enjoyed which the protagonist did not.

I have always so far enjoyed mono maniacal characters like the Count of Monte Cristo or perhaps even Howard Roark to an extent. Though in this case, I feel maybe a more rounded development might not be too bad. This is hard to digest but the book just goes on the show sometimes all your dedication and hardwork, integrity and dignity can add up to very little.

I don't know if that was the intention of the book, but that's what I got out of it.


EDIT : this book doesn't leave you easily, it also is a testament to the writer where the narrator keeps on talking big game and you keep on seeing through him.

Edit : Updated from 3 to 4 star. It takes time to sink in.

books.title: The Silent Patient
books.author: Alex Michaelides
books.review:
I did not think I would particularly enjoy this book and that reading it would be kind of a drag where I would have to force myself to it.

The reason for that was I had just read a book by Ishigo Kahuro and there was a huge discrepancy in level of writing or so I thought. also, quite simply the start is little trying.

The book does pick up quite well after the first 50 pages or so and although I don't agree with most of psychology mentioned in the book, it was a decent read.

End for me little Meh and to me it feels like having bit of loop holes.  I also think it would've been better for book to end few pages earlier than it did.

books.title: Spiritual Awakening, Vol. 1
books.author: Hit Premanand Govind Sharan Ji Maharaj
books.review:
Not for me. Not to mention , Description of hell and cause for it , wasn't pleasant for me. Suddenly seemed whoa, am I in the wrong.

But I think once you have read Gita and internalized some of it, this doesn't seem to hold that water.

Premanand Maharaj seems very jovial and may be enlightened , this book did not help in the way I anticipated.

books.title: White Nights
books.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
books.review:
I took this book up when I was particularly going through a reading rut and thought this would help me get back into reading habit again.

I had read Crime and Punishment and knew Dostoevsky is regarded as a genius. 

I have to say, this book did not resonate with me. It's just two short stories and any be they were more meaningful when they were written but not just for me kind of blah! 

The first story at least stirred up the emotions and I did not follow all arguments or point it at least touched a chord. The second one for me was so boring , I did not even attempt the following conversation completely.  

I guess my tastes and reading intellect aren't refined enough to read Russian Geniuses .

books.title: The Stars, Like Dust (Galactic Empire, #1)
books.author: Isaac Asimov
books.review:
I was stuck in a rot and had not read anything new in months and I needed an Author who would keep me gripped, Since I recalled most of Mario puzo's book and many of P.G.Wodehouse I decided instead to go with Asimov. I had fond memories of reading I, Robot and , Robots and Empire in my teens. So I was pretty confident of finishing my first new one for 2025.

The start was slow and but clumsy , the romance and love story between Arta and Biron seemed half baked and the book did not see to have good pacing.  Some of the actions and reasoning also seemed a bit far fetched and weird but the second half is the very book shines although it doesn't completely make up for everything it's not actually a drag. The end was a bit too cliched for lack of a better word.

books.title: A Damsel in Distress
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
Every time I am stuck and need to kick off my reading habit again, I pick Wodehouse and it usually does the trick. So after 6 months of break or so, I was able to get on the reading bandwagon thanks to this one.

Usually , I'll rate Wodehouse books on how often they make me chuckle out loud and how much I enjoyed reading them. Though there wasn't a case of the former in this one, I did enjoy reading it.

It has Earl of Marshmoreton which is like a slightly different version of Lord Elmsworth and lady Caroline is well like any of the sisters of Lords Elmsworth.

From Chivalry, to broken hearts, from young love to beautiful platonic friendship it seems to have everything. It even entertains an imposter a la Blandings castle style, well kind of.

books.title: The Decision Book: Fifty Models for Strategic Thinking
books.author: Mikael Krogerus
books.review:
I feel I got less out of this book than I got from secret and that's saying something.

Maybe a couple of lines on a random model didn't do it for me.

It just was not useful for me.

books.title: Full Moon (Blandings Castle, #7)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
I have always enjoyed Blanding's castle novel and Hon Galahad Threepwood is defn in top 3 of my Blanding's Castle character. So this book had me in good sprits. If you feel other books have shortchanged you of his presence then this one is definitely for you. 

This book is slight deviation from most blandings castle novel in which an imposter doesn't even stay a night at Blanding's castle and I felt Prudence definitely needed more presence the start was extremely promising. 

P.G.Wodehouse is perhaps the only author who books I actively re-read. This one I did not mind re-reading and I think it was just slightly that much better the second time around

books.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant: A Guide to Wealth and Happiness
books.author: Eric Jorgenson
books.review: Going in I knew exactly what would be there in the book and having heard Naval on several occasions I wasn't sure I would get anything more from it. But I did, some of his chapters and quotes are profound and I guess will stay with me for time to come. Primary among them, importance of reading.

books.title: Rework
books.author: Jason Fried
books.review:
I really admire Jason Fried , some of their thought process and their approach to software is somewhat refreshing.

The book has few good points but maybe that's about it. It is 220 pages of which may be you have to read 100 pages of which I would say perhaps 50 are not required. Some of them just seem over the top or not applicable or just kinda bizarre like the idea don't write down customers'r feedback or ask to enhance a product if it's important it would keep on coming again and again and you'll eventually remember it.

Meh!

books.title: Galahad at Blandings (Blandings Castle, #10)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
At first I was taken in by some of the reviews and was very excited about it. Then I thought it was ok but I had definitely read better Blanding's castle novel. By the end I was no longer miffed. 

It's a Blandings' novel just go for it.

books.title: Tell-Tale Brain: Tales of the Unexpected from Inside Your Mind
books.author: V.S. Ramachandran
books.review:
I realised that most of my book ratings tend to be 3. Even though internally I think of it as low 3 or high 3, it's still a 3. So now I am skipping three altogether and going with either 2 or 4.

With the above rationale, this was definitely 4 for me. As a layman I could not keep track of a lot of areas of the brain being talked about. I wished there was a small accompanying book with more diagrams , glossary and context for easier access.

But the core of the book, the cases, the discussion on self and especially art was very intriguing. 

It brings up many questions and at times I felt like shouting well why didn't you do that test.

books.title: The Hidden Hindu
books.author: Akshat Gupta
books.review:
I don't know why the Author had to make Abhilash as a bigot who hated people of certain religion. One person who was knowledgeable in Indian mythology was a bigot. It has nothing to do with the story , it doesn't go anywhere. Just to show a particular type of person (religious ) in bad light.

Book is ok with mish mash of theories we have heard and read. It has clearly taken a lot from 'Man from the Earth ' and some of the movies of Dr. Frankenstein s monster. It may achieve commercial success, but overall it's meh!

books.title: Mr. Everit's Secret: What I Learned from the World's Richest Man
books.author: Alan Cohen
books.review:
I was extremely excited about the book because the person who lent me the book was infectiously excited about it.

However, in reading the first few pages I realised it's not for me. There may come a time when it may be something I value, but right now I just don't see much value in it.

This feels like one of the or perhaps the only books I hate read.

books.title: ANDAMAN
books.author: Ratnadip Acharya
books.review:
At first I was a little disappointed with the writing. Perhaps I was just being too snooty. It really gripped me after the first few pages. 

Learning and understanding Sazaye Kaali Pani probably remains my favorite part of the book. It was also a bit dark and possibly emotionally draining. This feels like the Indian holocaust which is not talked about enough.

The second part of the book was ok I feel. The book totters towards true vengeance and then just perhaps takes a step back, I feel the author could not commit on that path. From moral perspective actions on ross Island were not correct I feel. 

Also bringing back Niladri and not having anything out of it was also weird. Like it was not needed. 


All in all , I did enjoy reading the book.

books.title: Sputnik Sweetheart
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.review:
Murakami books don't often have standard ends but this book is no Norwegian Woods or Kafka on the shore. It is just plainly meh, writing with his sheer writing capability made a readable story of few characters with a very thin plotline and very little magical realism.

A few things I felt very definitely missed in translation. I say this, because more than a couple of sentences did not mean anything. They appeared deep but seemed to me like gibberish.

Perhaps only book worse than After Dark from Murakami.

books.title: Origin (Robert Langdon, #5)
books.author: Dan    Brown
books.review:
I have always hated people who liked to make fun of Dan Brown's book and his formula. I always enjoyed them. It had that gripping quality to make me feel intrigued at first and content by end of the book.

And with Dan Brown steering away slightly from his formula in Inferno, I was excited for this one. But this was painfully formulaic and no new concepts introduced, no noetic science to know about, no great secret society. 

This one actually looks like someone might have parodied one of his other books. It seems painfully low effort. Disappointed with Dan Brown on this one.

Merged review:

I have always hated people who liked to make fun of Dan Brown's book and his formula. I always enjoyed them. It had that gripping quality to make me feel intrigued at first and content by end of the book.

And with Dan Brown steering away slightly from his formula in Inferno, I was excited for this one. But this was painfully formulaic and no new concepts introduced, no noetic science to know about, no great secret society. 

This one actually looks like someone might have parodied one of his other books. It seems painfully low effort. Disappointed with Dan Brown on this one.

books.title: A Pelican at Blandings (Blandings Castle, #11)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: A pure Blandings novel rarely disappoints and even less know in the presence of Galahd Threepwood. It was a pleasant read and I was thinking I did not chuckle as I often do in other Blandings novel, but damn it, if it did not have me smiling reading last few pages.

books.title: Elon Musk
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.review:
It was more or less as expected. I was a bit disappointed that an anecdote (Elon solved an issue in Oracle or something like that)  got me excited about reading the book was just that much and not many more such examples could be found.

But overall as expected. Linearity or chapter sequence I feel could've been better.

books.title: The Giver (The Giver, #1)
books.author: Lois Lowry
books.review:
My review cannot be objective because evidently this a children's book and in spite of my behavior I am not. So I did not enjoy this book as much , I thought it would be a typical dystopian book which it was but probably lacked the gruesomeness which I had expected.

Overall it's not badly written. Set up is quite clear, story line very linear and thing
s are introduced timely. End was little wishy washy but I don't think it had any major impact on how I felt about book. Not a bad read for targeted audience.

books.title: The Case Of The Worried Waitress (Perry Mason, #77)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner
books.review:
Left disappointed by the Perry Mason series on HBO, I decided to turn to the trusted books which I had read perhaps 2 decades back. Although not as  good as I remembered them, it did not disappoint.

I usually like how everything wraps in the end. Though here I must admit, I missed a few revelations and never really understood who did the original crime.

Though I consider Saturday evening relatively well spent.

Rerated it to two. Because I still don't understand what triggered everything.

books.title: The Case of the Howling Dog (Perry Mason, #4)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner
books.review:
This was my 3rd Perry Mason book in a month and definitely a better one compared to the other two.

 The story was choesive and probable. One would get parts of it and still not others, so it is a bit more enjoyable than some of the other ones where no one could've predicted any of the events.

books.title: The Case of the Lame Canary (Perry Mason, #11)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner
books.review:
Maybe I am too old for this now but I was trying to relive the magic I felt when I read this in my teens.

This in particular was ok, strictly ok. I did not like the deduction and the ending felt far too rushed.

books.title: The Murder on the Links (Hercule Poirot, #2)
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.review:
I have never been a very big fan of Poirot but his books are good for leisure reading or getting back into the habit of reading.

The Reveal had layers but one of them is not easily digestible. Not very realistic, looking back at events some of them seem illogical.

But as all Agathe Christie's books it's a swift read and I enjoyed the time I spent reading it.

books.title: Revolutionaries: The Other Story of How India Won Its Freedom
books.author: Sanjeev Sanyal
books.review:
I would say in some sense this is a typical Sanjeev Sanyal read, absolutely replete with information. 

Few chapters felt long, especially the Ghadarite network and following the journey of one person is not easy as it scattered across chapters and events but then that's how life and history are.

A few chapters and events like Kaali Paani , Story of Ullaskar Dutt, Jallian walla Bagh are amazing. I am also embarrassed of not knowing a few key people who helped living me in independent India.

books.title: Child 44 (Leo Demidov, #1)
books.author: Tom Rob Smith
books.review:
It was after a long time that I read and enjoyed a murder mystery. I was bored with the entire premise but suddenly when I heard about this book set in the backdrop of Stalin's Russia, I had to give it a try.

The first chapter was too powerful for me to not complete the book. 

I don't want to go into details of who committed the murder or it's relatively simplistic plot but the main attraction of the book is a view into how Russian intelligence  worked then.

Thoroughly enjoyed the book, some parts were just heart wrenching.

books.title: The Bhagavad Gita
books.author: Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa
books.review:
Obviously, I'll refrain from actually trying to review Bhagavad Gita. I would say Bibek Debroy's stuff does come across quite a bit honest.

1: The only place I had an issue with translation was perhaps using Atman, for jivatma and Parmatma ( though clarified in footnotes)
2: Footnotes are awesome and at places I missed them, this is usually not the case. 


Think about it, you can read Bhagavad Gita in less than a day :-)

books.title: Samanya Dharma – Ethical Duties Common to All
books.author: Nithin Sridhar
books.review:
It's ok. I wanted to like it more than I eventually did. The first few pages are good but the core of the book talks about which books Vedas, upanishad, smriti of Hinduism mention which act as Samanya Dharm. 

Not having intimate details about underlying Vedas and other books, I would not know what to prioritise.

Though I don't regret reading it , it's a small book which might have changed my attitude towards something for good.

books.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles (Hercule Poirot, #1)
books.author: Agatha Christie

books.title: One Good Deed (Archer, #1)
books.author: David Baldacci
books.review:
I was hankering for a thriller murder mystery novel and was suggested this book by the guy at book store. Never having read this particular author's book I wasn't sure but went ahead with it.

I felt the start was slow and wasn't sure if it would keep me engaged enough to read 580 odd pages, but held it's own.

End was particularly Swift and tied up things nicely. There were a few instances which seemed just too much of coincidence or kind of action by protaganist you would not expect in such novels but all in all not too bad.

Had decent fun reading it. Though I am not sure I'll go for other books by the author.

books.title: Hot Water
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: Not set in Blandings castle, though it very well could've been it's about Chateau Bliisac and imposters there.  So, there are definite parallels. But all in all no a bad read. Classic Wodehouse.

books.title: KARMA YOGA by Swami Vivenkananda
books.author: Vivekananda
books.review:
I am not very learned on the spiritual thing and so lot of the text could've gone over my head. But I loved the first chapter but the second chapter ruined it for me absolutely. I did not get in what sense word nonresistance was used and even the analogies were bad. There are a few decent chapters after that, but by then I was in a rush to complete it so missed. The last 2 chapters were decent and first chapter is amazing. 

But it's a fairly small book and you might as well give it a thought. It also mentioned Christ, Mohammad, and Buddha to an extent. So it may have broader appeal. 

In terms of Karma Yoga, a lot of the ideas do seem to come from Gita, It's not always easy to digest all but it does seem to extend the concept of Karma yoga little more than one would seem to get from Bhagavad Gita

books.title: The Psychology of Money: Timeless Lessons on Wealth, Greed, and Happiness
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.review:
For large part I thought it was ok. It reinforced some of the beliefs I had and few things I did not agree or thought contradictory. 

Overall I think day spent reading it was probably well spent.

One new idea it put in my mind which I think makes it all the more valuable is the bit about point of having money is to control what you do with your team.

books.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy (Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, #1)
books.author: Douglas Adams
books.review: I can't believe I waited so long to read this book. At times it gets just too bizarre and unrealistic. Author doesn't even try to make you believe it can be true. But the genius part of it is there and unparalleled. The series easily goes to one of my favorites.

books.title: The Ocean of Churn: How the Indian Ocean Shaped Human History
books.author: Sanjeev Sanyal

books.title: The Will to Meaning: Foundations and Applications of Logotherapy
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl

books.title: India in the Age of Ideas: Select Writings: 2006-2018
books.author: Sanjeev Sanyal
books.review:
I really want good reads to give me ability to rate something 3.5. 3 for me as on par and 4 for me is having enjoyed it. This one falls somewhere in between. 

I picked it because Sanjeev Sanyal is one of my favorite writers and Land of Seven Rivers was an absolutely amazing book and I enjoy his videos on YouTube and getting his perspective on things. So going in I was fully aware that since this is just collection of his writing I would be reading stuff I have either already read or heard in his interviews. This was precisely the case, but I wanted it available in print and to read it all at go, so I am happy with my purchase and Sanyal remains somewhat of thought leader to me. 

 Book is split in three different parts, his writings on History and Culture, Urban Dynamics and Economics. I enjoyed the first part most, followed by second and just quickly wrapped up on economics which if somewhat ironic considering he is the Principal Economic Advisor in the ministry of finance which makes him a full time economist. 

My one ask/ disappointment was that it doesn't include white papers that we may have published. One on risk which is pinned on his twitter feed was pretty great. 

All in all, if you are Sanyal fan you know what you are getting.

books.title: Quichotte
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.review:
Typical Salman Rushdie book in some sense.

Magical Realism - Check
Connection to India - Check
Literary Style - Check

Some comments about mistreatment of Muslims in India stung a bit considering they were largely incorrect and hit close to home. But that's just me. This time disparaging comments were less subtle.

Did not enjoy it as much as Shalimar the Clown or Enchantress of Florence but overall not a bad read.

Ending could've been bit more polished.

books.title: After Dark
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.review:
This book was huge disappoint for me, not only is it nowhere close to some of other work by author like Norwegian Wood, 1Q84,  Kafka on the shore but there is just nothing there. There is a set up and then that's it. 

There was very little aspect of magical realism, there were no resolved arcs this was like a pilot episode of a show trying to get on air. One potentially intriguing thread that could have been developed. But really first few pages has a set up and then banality associated with it.

I refuse to believe any great literary work is present here.

books.title: The Secret Garden
books.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
books.review: A book I came across and read bit too late for I was in my late teens when I read this children's book. But now in my mid 30s I still remember about it. It has to have something special about it.

books.title: Joy in the Morning (Jeeves, #8)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
I went back to Jeeves and Wooster after along time. It may well have some of Wodehouse magic but having read so many of his Blandings Novel this seems to fall bit short.

Fun read nonetheless.

books.title: The Last Lecture
books.author: Randy Pausch
books.review:
This is the second time I read this book. First time I read it in 2013 and now when I read it again about 7 years later I was surprised of how many anecdotes and points I had remembered from the book. 

It's a decent read and I didn't mind spending better part of my Saturday afternoon on the book.

books.title: Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones
books.author: James Clear
books.review:
I knew what this book would be about while starting it and while I am usually not fond of self help books this one was more pragmatic. One of the few self helps I did not regret reading. 

Few things may be common sense or obvious but reading them in context and understanding magnitude of its effect can motivate you.

It did make me more conscious of few things I am doing. So all in all a decent read worth Investing time in.

books.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.review:
Finally Done !!! This is a book that's long been on my reading list and even on my shelf and it is almost exactly what I anticipated it would be. Having read Homo Deus and 21 lessons I knew what I was getting myself into. 

I am not gonna lie after first few pages pace drops considerable and it seems bit like a drag but then last one fifty pages or so come back with a vengeance.

It's seems very difficult for me to read his work and not have my mind blown away by sometimes seemingly simple conclusion or an observation.

Beautiful !!!

books.title: Fahrenheit 451
books.author: Ray Bradbury
books.review:
I did not like this book, it could be because I read it many many years after it was written or may be because I am not target audience. But this dystopia novel just fell short of my expectations. I feel I have read better written YA dystopian novels. Primarily because I just did not find writing appealing. Themes are vague, story has flaky end and characters are rarely intriguing. Comparing this with 1984 I can say that they don't belong on same level. We don't have enough insight into world and far too much of logic is leap is taken from one aspect to current state in that universe

However, the concept was intriguing and that's what led me to reading in first place. Also, as many would say book was indeed prophetic in some sense, it highlighted issues with social media usage even before social media came into existence.

books.title: Dracula
books.author: Bram Stoker
books.review:
As such this book is over a century old and so suffers from some limitations nand drawbacks of time in which it was written.

But reading it leaves one with clear understanding why this is considered a classic and still in circulation.

It sometimes seems illogical, and some times seems repetitive but some times it seems very smart overall it's not a book I could put down easily.

books.title: The Krishna Key
books.author: Ashwin Sanghi
books.review: Start is kinda bad after 50 off pages I just left reading and then picked up after deciding I need to be more patient with it. It definitely has Dan Brown's Da Vinci thing going on but actions of characters and monologues are just so incredibly unbelievable. End is also meh! Only saving grace is interesting tid bits about Hindu mythology. Some of them even if outlandish are fun to read others are even a step ahead of conspiracy theories. Logic jumps are just not easily digestible.

books.title: Krishna's Secret
books.author: Devdutt Pattanaik
books.review: I read it because it was a recommendation and wanted to check it out. It's more like an article hardly 30-40 pages. You may learn something here and there but nothing especially in new, then again it's included in prime and takes only like half an hour. Has some nice depictions.

books.title: Keepers of the Kalachakra
books.author: Ashwin Sanghi
books.review:
It's been sometime since I read a thriller, when I started reading it, a thought went through my mind, ah shit, here we go again. With the usual tricks and loopholes of thrillers but it actually became bit more interesting as it went along. 

The interesting part of the book is obviously religious aspect of HInduism and Buddhism.It does this quite well in the middle of book. Towards end however it brings in way too concepts and muddles the water quite a bit. Twists are ok and predictable. 

Over all I do not regret reading book and may even take up his one of the other books with similar theme.

books.title: Ikigai: The Japanese Secret to a Long and Happy Life
books.author: Héctor  García
books.review:
The book was ok for most part. It has a chapter on logotherapy which was largely redundant for me, considering Man's search for meaning is one of my favorite books. Other things can be considered common knowledge large part BUT and here is the thing BUT sometimes in life it is necessary to be reminded of common sense things which we do not follow. 

There are short notes from people who have lived over 100 years and a section on exercise which for me was largely useless .

They hyped the concept of IKGAI and the entire book isn't on it. But I still did not mind reading it, one good insight to lead a healthy life can go long way. 

It's barely 170 (smaller than average) page book which can be easily completed in couple of hours. Al in all did not mind reading the book

books.title: Land of the Seven Rivers: A Brief History of India's Geography
books.author: Sanjeev Sanyal
books.review:
I have to admit I am not a history or a geography buff and bought the book only for love of the author. I have to say Sanjeev did not disappoint. 

At points it was tedious to understand all the geographic locations, some common but unknown to me, so unknown to most. BUT and it is a big BUT but the sense and feelings that it evokes in you as you read some of the passages and understand some of the history was totally worth the constant trip to google maps. 

One downside though is because it is content heavy I did not retain much after the book was finished, but the upside is it gives me a chance to try and revisit the book again.

books.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.review:
I started the book in 2017 and then read half and lost the track and later book itself. It is defn an above average book. I wasn't very happy with translation , some mistakes could be spotted rather easily. 
Overall, it was a little let down, because of hype surrounding it. End was fantastic

books.title: The Valmiki Ramayana Vol. 3
books.author: Vālmīki
books.review:
I don't want to rate Valmiki's Ramayana. So I'll not concentrate on content but other things

*One of the things I missed was detailed chapter list. It had chapters and Kand but that makes searching something very difficult. So If I want to read just about fight between Lakshaman and Meghnad it's not easy. Even more so because text has so many name for different people you cannot even easily search on kindle. 

*This book includes Uttara Kand which per some sources is a later addition. 

*Overall I am good having read it, but I might have got same from  ValmikiRamayan.net

books.title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams
books.author: Matthew Walker
books.review:
I doubt my review matters here, especially since you see Bill Gates having written a  good one here. But  here goes nothing. 

This was by most measures an excellent book. Just enough of science and takeaway. There was may be one instance where I felt it was slightly repetitive and I can skip it but apart from that it was pleasant read.

One thing I wish author had added some study or test to see effects of oversleeping, it is mentioned no such data exists but even highlighting a study where no effect of oversleeping is seen would have been  good

books.title: The Mahabharata: Volume 1
books.author: Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa
books.review:
When I heard about critical edition, I was happy and wanted to read this immediately and I am glad I read it.

But if you are a casual reader, you must remember It's not meant to be read like a novel largely. 
It is an Epic. 

The first few chapters with a description of lineages and family trees are excruciating in detail and it just doesn't seem very feasible to digest it all. The story started with Arjun's grandson Parikshit's son and it takes time to reach the meat and bones of parts that we are familiar with.

But it's Mahabharat. I cannot review it, it is what it is.

books.title: Man's Search for Meaning
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl
books.review:
The book is divided into 2 main parts. 

The first part is the author's experience and understanding of Human Psyche from concentration camps in Nazi Germany. The second part talks more about Logotherapy.

In the beginning, I wanted to get through concentration camp parts because I did not want to read of the horrors of the holocaust. But the more I read more I was taken in by the first part of the book.

When I started with the second part, I thought I will not enjoy it because I would invariably read something I do not agree or understand, and although I am a novice in reading philosophy and psychology and I did not understand some of it. I can attest there are a few lines that are extremely powerful. Few lines just gave me a euphoric feeling similar to what one would get after a workout or having a great load removed from your shoulder.

This is perhaps the only book I have read in the last decade which I am considering re-reading.


EDIT : 

I did read it the second time.

books.title: As a Man Thinketh
books.author: James Allen
books.review:
This is a very small book, almost like a magazine article. I suppose this book is one of the main inspirations for the entire genre of self-help books that have taken over the entire generation of readers. 

The author does well to hammer a point home, without taking 100 pages to do so.  I am not much of a self-help kind of person, even though I might be who needs the most. I'm glad though, my self-help was James Allen's As a man thinketh and not Robin Sharma's drivel.

books.title: Young Men in Spats
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
This is my only PG WODEHOUSE book with 2 stars. It is not because I can compare it with other 2 stars books, but inherently I have come to expect more of Wodehouse books. 

This is a collection of short stories, mostly around Pongo Twistleton and one more chap. But hardly any stories strikeout, only one I truly enjoyed was one with Uncle Fred, that character is a gem. 

I read it on my 3rd attempt mostly because of lockdown, give this one a miss and pick up another Blandings novel

books.title: 21 Lessons for the 21st Century
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.review:
I had read reviews and realized lot of things in books are repeated from Homo Deus and Sapiens but I was ok with that and the book turned out to be pretty much what I expected.

Few things :

1: This is not a self-help or instructional book in the traditional sense
2: This is more like 21 essays on different topics, some you will agree with and some you will not care about 
3: I skimmed through some and perused others based on my interests, I am assuming that it would be true for others too.
4: The first ( technological challenge ) and the last one ( resilence ) were probably the ones that resonated the most with me.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.review:
This was one of the books which when I picked expected to be quite good, and it appeared promising at the beginning then it became very slow and I thought I was going to be disappointed but by the end, it was indeed quite good so all in all I did not regret picking it up, the end particularly was riveting.

It did take me quite a bit to get through the book, and I think I did not give the attention it deserves or read it the way it is meant to be, sometimes the transitions were quite abrupt for me leading me to forget where was this offshoot from.

Overall the writing quality is above average and well it's pretty good.

books.title: Uncle Dynamite
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: Enjoyed it. Blanding castles are usually my favorite ones, but gotta say Lord Ickenham is no less than Hon Gallahad.

books.author: George Orwell
books.review:
Considerably more darker than Animal Farm. I also enjoyed it less, primarily because it has little story and just mostly dystopia and philosophy behind it. What little story it has also has great unexplainable leaps. 

But a powerful book nonetheless.

books.title: The Case of the Calendar Girl (Perry Mason, #57)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner
books.review:
Pretty much what you would expect. This was a blast from the past for me.

My book had last page or two torn out so that was annoying.

books.title: Homo Deus: A History of Tomorrow
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.review:
Not being acquainted with the author's previous work I wasn't sure how I would receive this book. I think I have to agree with most people on this, Yuval Harari is clearly a gifted writer and possibly one of the thought leaders of today's time on humanity. 

There are aspects of the book when I felt it was too repetitive or comparison which was just not needed. But the data points, studies, history and it's implication had me hooked. I regret trying to read this loke a fiction book and not giving it more attention than it deserved. Part of the reason, I treated it mentally as fiction novel is because I did not agree with some of the conclusion, it could have been more cohesive in thought

Overall a worthy read.

books.title: Against the Gods: The Remarkable Story of Risk
books.author: Peter L. Bernstein

books.title: The Four: The Hidden DNA of Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google
books.author: Scott Galloway
books.review:
This is a book which was written in 2017 but feels like it was written in 2010 because so much has transpired in the last couple of years book just comes as outdated. 

Predictably, it talks about the big 4 four, but it leaves out the juicy details it doesn't have anything that you don't already know if you are a regular consumer of news about these companies. I expected more insight into tech companies and their flouting of rules, Cambridge Analytica scandal, hit pieces by NYT on Kalanick, movies on Steve Jobs do a better job of shedding light on these companies than the book.

I did enjoy some insights on retails and advertising by the author.

books.title: Summer Lightning (Blandings Castle, #4)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: One of the best P.G.Wodehouse Blanding's castle work. Enough said

books.title: Five Point Someone: What Not to Do at IIT
books.author: Chetan Bhagat

books.title: Something Fresh (Blandings Castle, #1)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: After reading 'Summer Lightning', Blanding's castle stories have become my new favorite, even surpassing Jeeves. This one is not as good as Full Moon or Summer Lightning but it is the book where we are introduced to Lord Emsworth, and for that alone it might be worth a read.

books.title: Rich Dad's Cashflow Quadrant: Rich Dad's Guide to Financial Freedom
books.author: Robert T. Kiyosaki

books.title: Illusions: The Adventures of a Reluctant Messiah
books.author: Richard Bach

books.title: The Mahabharata Secret
books.author: Christopher C. Doyle
books.review:
Of course, the title drew me in.

It's like a Dan Brown book with a secret to be unfolded but based in India. Writing does fall short of the mark when compared to Brown. But the premise was not all too bad, some twists were so obvious they should not have been present at all.  There are few characters which are absolutely not needed and editing could've been better, but overall I don't regret reading it through.

books.title: Service With a Smile
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review:
Yes another Blandings castle novel. This time its Lord Ickenham who goes around creating chaos and servicing people with a smile. 

I did find humor lacking a little bit compared to best of Wodehouse but it's an easy read and no regrets on reading it.

One of those rare Wodehouse book where you actually have an antagonist.

books.title: Kalki Purana
books.author: B.K. Chaturvedi
books.review: I read this because I had it, and ordered it because I thought it would be an interesting read. It was not, it was terrible. I don't even remember any storyline from it, the book was weak there was nothing spiritual or remotely awakening about it. Frankly, I think I wasted a couple of hours trying to finish it, which I should not have. I just skimmed through it quickly and fell asleep in between.

books.title: A Column of Fire (Kingsbridge, #3)
books.author: Ken Follett
books.review: Good insight in religious malevolence of 15th century Europe

books.title: Big Money
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: It's a P.G.Wodehouse novel. Perhaps the one of only a few or the only one where there is active use of gat to hold up people. Action in a Wodehouse novel, can you imagine it .

books.title: The Old Man and the Sea
books.author: Ernest Hemingway
books.review:
It has a few powerful lines, It's a very small book so you would not lose a lot of time even if you did not like it. Having said that, I have found that I don't particularly care for a lot of classics or all-time best books.

It obviously uses language associated with boats which can be difficult to comprehend for someone like me who knows nothing about boats. So if it's not something you want to deal with, you can give it a miss. A lot of people find a lot of hidden messages and powerful metaphor from the book but lot of it is hogwash if you read for pleasure as I do, it doesn't matter much.

books.title: Dune (Dune #1)
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.review: Went in with very high expectations, found it to be an ok book. To really get into the dune universe I'll have to dedicate a lot more time reading other books and you miss a lot of stuff in the first read so a second read might be warranted. I'm glad I read it, so I can check it off my list now, but don't think will be reading the rest of the books set in this universe.

books.title: Of Counsel
books.author: Arvind Subramanian
books.review:
I am going to be little partial to the book and rate it a tad higher than I would normally have ...

This book has no spicy gossip or inside information on modi or Jaitley. I kind of appreciate it, that Author did not cheap out and indulge mindless gossip.

It also has almost no information on DeMo  except for 2 thoughts post it. There is considerably more detail on GST, as he was more involved in it.

Few chapters on Federer and Nadal are a complete miss and should have been left out of it.


There was considerable information on fiscal deficit, primary deficit most of which I did not follow and May have to re read it.

books.title: The Girl in Blue
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: As with most Wodehouse book, this one too brought a smile on face now and then. Perhaps not as exciting as Blandings Castle stories or as twisted as Jeeves, but a good read nonetheless. This is perhaps one of the few Wodehouse books I have read, which perhaps has a bad guy (If one can call a pretty girl looking to marry rich that ) to speak of, I certainly don't remember any others to speak of.

books.title: Shunya
books.author: Sri M.
books.review: It is a small book, which can be easily finished in one sitting. There are good aspects of a book, the main easy flowing storyline and it seems to be nicely written. However, Shunya the protagonist keeps on saying he is nothing, void and keeps on performing miracles which are kind antithetical to being nothing. Also, there is no takeaway from the book. When you read something like Alchemist on magical surrealism/ self help book, it gives some message, finds your destiny, believe in yourself, trusts yourself, gave up material possession, this one has no takeaway. I don't regret reading it though.

books.title: Good Omens: The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch
books.author: Terry Pratchett

books.title: The Palace of Illusions
books.author: Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni
books.review: Not bad, a breezy read. It could have been a good children's book if Author did not sway into make it little edgier.

books.title: The Peshwa: The Lion and the Stallion
books.author: Ram Sivasankaran
books.review:
I primarily read it because it was free as part of Kindle first and it popped up. It's set in a time period of Shahu Maharaj's reign where they have an uneasy alliance with Mughals in Delhi. Few parts of it were really good and language is really easy to follow through ( except perhaps sometimes the confusing usage of titles and names). But there are huge gaps which go unmentioned like there is a new vazir in Delhi, Maratha's key ally goes missing and Peshwa doesn't take any notice of it? 

I don't know if it's intentional or unintentional but a lot of Peshwa's thing is shown to be in the grey area rather than all white ( nepotism over meritocracy, limited notion of respect for Chhatrapati, SPOILER: Peshwa's choices to let Nizam live twice. 

I don't think I'll be reading the sequel ( if it comes out ) which would be focused on Mastani.

books.title: The Case of the Counterfeit Eye (Perry Mason, #6)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner

books.title: The Case of the Bigamous Spouse (Perry Mason, #65)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner

books.title: The Case of the Lucky Legs (Perry Mason, #3)
books.author: Erle Stanley Gardner

books.title: Sidney Sheldon’s The Silent Widow
books.author: Tilly Bagshawe
books.review:
It's been some time since I read a Sidney Sheldoniiish book. Overall the book was OK, It did have certain Sidney Sheldon flavor to it. I am not sure how this works advertising the book on the name of the deceased author. 

As for the book itself, Not bad, was easy to go through in terms of suspects and plot it is a little thin

books.title: Life over Two Beers and other stories
books.author: Sanjeev Sanyal
books.review: I am not usually a big fan of short stories, but I picked up this book in rather hurry just because of the author's youtube videos. Fortunately, I wasn't too disappointed with the book even if it was just a collection of short stories.  As usually happens some stories were very powerful ( Books ) and some perhaps not so much (Reunion) but overall I am glad I picked it up. It has that easy going quality like that of Sudha Murthy books and touch a raw nerve every now and then.

books.title: Asura: Tale Of The Vanquished, The Story of Ravana and His People
books.author: Anand Neelakantan
books.review:
Book has no saving grace. I wanted it to be good, really good but I can find nothing which I can hold on to. I liked Immortals of Meluha trilogy and  Palace of Illusion which seem to have a similar format. The difference between Asura and those books is that this one is written rather poorly. You can find several typos, several words which seem out of place for the tone of the book.

It takes a grand mythological story and absolutely butchers it. It tries to show everyone has human having human faults, but it has major loopholes. Sita being spitting image of Mandodri and her daughter, yet not a single conversation is recorded between them. Bhadra is just everywhere, he is the only one who seems to have changed the course of history multiple times and in ways is shown more powerful and Intelligent than the protagonist ( and perhaps the antagonist ). The whole brahmin, caste implication was just too annoying. Vibhishan's character is completely destroyed he goes from a useless, ambitionless bookworm, to a conniving sociopath. I can go on and on about it, but at end of the day, I'd rather read Blan Scion of Ishkvaku rather than this drivel.

books.title: In the Shadow of the Banyan
books.author: Vaddey Ratner

books.title: Kafka on the Shore
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.review:
This was my third Murakami book after 1Q84 and Norwegian Wood. After reading this is not a bad book, I can safely say, I am not a very big fan of Murakami. 

I did not understand all the hoopla over this book, it's an ok book with an ok plot.

books.title: Norwegian Wood
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.review: There is little to no point in reviewing a book which is over 30 years old and considered a classic by many. Good Characters, So many wild ways the book could have gone, it opens up so many plotlines but at end of it all, it is a straightforward love story with a vague ending. It has a certain very apparent Catcher in the Rye quality to it.

books.title: Leave It to Psmith (Psmith, #4 ; Blandings Castle, #2)
books.author: P.G. Wodehouse
books.review: Go for it.

books.title: Mossad: The Greatest Missions of the Israeli Secret Service
books.author: Michael Bar-Zohar
books.review: The timeline is little messy and it's very disjoint in chronology. But nonetheless, delivers on what it promises

books.author: Peter Wohlleben

books.author: Amish Tripathi
books.review: Ok. Only Setup, Ends with Kidnapping of Sita

books.author: Sachin Tendulkar

books.author: Alice Sebold
books.review: Gaaaa

books.title: The Sceptical Patriot: Exploring the Truths Behind the Zero and Other Indian Glories
books.author: Sidin Vadukut

books.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (Harry Potter, #6)
books.author: J.K. Rowling

books.title: This Book Does Not Exist
books.author: Mike  Schneider
books.review:
When I bought nexus -7 I wanted to read a good book on tablet to see how I would like reading digital books ( not pdfs..:P ). So I went ahead and bought kindle version of the book 'This book does not exist' as it had good reviews.

Book is new age fiction book with heavy presence of social networking sites like facebook and twitter, it also has a link to youtube video, which is part of the story. (This was a definite plus of having a kindle version of book, video was embedded and had to use just one click to watch it. I would have ignored it if I had the paperback edition ).

I found presence of social networking sites bit annoying, and being from different background than the intended audience of this book ( Americans and Europeans ) I missed lot of references to pop culture. But overall book is refreshing .

If I would have written a book, I could imagine it to be very much on the same lines as this book. It depicts everything in a very surreal manner, and since it has so many references including a video, it makes you feel as if you are reading story or blog by your friend and not a fiction novel. 

Ending was little bland , but overall I can give it 6.5 of 10.

books.author: Markus Zusak
books.review: I felt let down .Period. Cannot say more without spoilers

books.title: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe (The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, #2)
books.author: Douglas Adams
books.review: Because you are bombarded with lot of new information throughout the series its sometimes easy to lose track of the main story line. I think was probably the best book of the series, the one which had most crazy thoughts and made me laugh the most..

books.title: Operation Karakoram
books.author: Arvind Nayar
books.review:
I find it weird that this book did not have any discussion or reviews. Granted, It is not best of the books even by an Indian author. But it is I find much better than other run on the mill Indian books.

This to me was like a Jeffery Archer /Sydney Sheldon book but based on/in India.

books.title: Mostly Harmless (Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, #5)
books.author: Douglas Adams
books.review:
I concur with most of the reviews here..and it almost felt as if it wasn't written by the same person .

It did not provide complete sense of closure..Read through it just for sense of completion.
